news.title: Vietnam U15 bounce back with two straight wins at 2026 World Cup
news.lede: Vietnam's U15 team began their campaign with a 6-3 defeat to Bosnia-Herzegovina but quickly found their rhythm under head coach Hoang Anh Tuan. Their first victory came against Brunei, with Vietnam securing a commanding 6-0 win to collect their first points of the tournament. The young Vietnamese players carried that momentum into their next group-stage match against Mauritius at 8 p.m. on October 25. Combining proactive attacking play with solid defending, Vietnam produced another convincing performance to win 4-1.

news.title: Kenya too strong as Samoa complete difficult FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Samoa have ended their FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup campaign after losing 4-0 to Kenya in Morocco. The defeat at the Mohammed VI Football Academy in Salé completed a difficult tournament for the Oceania representatives, who conceded 28 goals in three Group E matches. Kenya made a flying start, taking the lead after only four minutes through Mwanakombo Bakari. The Junior Starlets dominated possession and kept Samoa’s defence under pressure throughout the opening half.

news.title: Under-15 team pick up two wins at World Cup in Azerbaijan
news.lede: Bermuda’s under-15 football team have made a fantastic start to the World Cup in Azerbaijan with two wins from their opening their group matches. Bermuda opened their campaign with a 5-0 win over British Virgin Islands, with goals from Adam Barritt, Darien Lambert, Chaz Edmead, Stephen Astwood and De’Ari Trott giving the young Gombey Warriors a fantastic start to the competition. They were then unlucky in their second game, losing 1-0 to Georgia and playing the entire second half a player short after Asa Trew-Smith was sent off in the twentieth minute. It was only in the last minute that Bermuda conceded with Danieli Gurtskaia breaking hearts.

news.title: FIFA's Infantino claims 'vast majority' support before election
news.lede: FIFA's embattled president Gianni Infantino said he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of football despite his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. Infantino is seeking re-election next year in the face of attempts to force him to stand down following the divisive plan. He infuriated football leaders in Europe, North America and Asia over the proposal to sell profits in the World Cup through a commercial subsidiary. But in an interview released on Saturday with the BBC at the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, Infantino brushed off calls for him to step down.
